LESSON: READING 2.2.1 INTENSIVE READING

Grade: SNE  /  physical-impairment / Grade six
Subject: ENGLISH
Strand: Strand 2
Topic 2.2: Reading 2.2.1 Intensive Reading
Suggested lessons in curriculum: 2

SECTION 1: INTRODUCTION

This lesson covers Reading 2.2.1 Intensive Reading, part of Strand 2 in SNE  /  physical-impairment / Grade six ENGLISH.

Key inquiry question: Why do we enjoy reading stories and poems? 2. Which stories and poems have you read?

You will study the official KICD learning outcomes, classroom activities, values, and competencies for this topic. Use Kenyan examples from your county, school, and community throughout.

SECTION 2: LEARNING OUTCOMES

By the end of this topic, you should be able to:

Refer to the KICD curriculum reference at the end of this lesson for the full list of outcomes.

SECTION 3: KEY CONCEPTS AND EXPLANATION

A. Suggested learning experiences (from KICD)

1.  in purposive groups, read a poem or story and identify the characters and events,  Read a story of about 500 words and predict the events then answer factual and inferential questions. Learners with speech difficulties could use residual speech/ digital devices with text- 1.

SECTION 4: LEARNING ACTIVITIES

A. At school

1.  in purposive groups, read a poem or story and identify the characters and events,  Read a story of about 500 words and predict the events then answer factual and inferential questions. Learners with speech difficulties could use residual speech/ digital devices with text- 1.

B. At home with your parent or guardian

1. Read this lesson on Reading 2.2.1 Intensive Reading together.
2. Discuss the key inquiry question and give examples from your area.
3. Write five sentences summarising what you learned.
4. Prepare for the revision quiz at the end of this topic.

SECTION 5: CORE COMPETENCIES, VALUES, AND PCIs

Core Competencies to be developed:
 Communication and Collaboration: The learner’s ability to recognise the value of others opinions is enhanced as they work

with peers to describe characters or events in poems and stories.

 Creativity and Imagination: The learner undertakes tasks that encourage artistic expression of ideas while creating

crossword puzzles using learnt vocabulary.

Values:
Respect is promoted as learner appreciates the opinion of others while collaborating with peers to recite a poem.

Pertinent and Contemporary Issues:
(PCIs):

Life Skills Education (Self-awareness): The learner becomes aware of their capability as they practise effective communication

through proficiency in reading.

Link to other Subjects

The skill of predicting events in a story is relevant in the concept of storytelling in Religious Education.
